Sustain
sŭs-tān´
v. (to hold up, bear, nourish; rendering Hebrew kul and samak)
Latin sustinere, to hold up from beneath. The Hebrew kul is to contain and so to provide for; the widow who sustained Elijah did it with a barrel.

Biblical Definition

“Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved” (Psa 55:22). To Elijah: “get thee to Zarephath… behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee” (1Ki 17:9). Of the wilderness: “forty years didst thou sustain them in the wilderness, so that they lacked nothing; their clothes waxed not old” (Neh 9:21). “The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; but a wounded spirit who can bear?” (Pro 18:14). David: “I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me” (Psa 3:5). Isaac of Jacob: “with corn and wine have I sustained him” (Gen 27:37).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines sustain as to bear; to uphold; to support; to hold suspended; to keep from sinking in despondence; to maintain, to keep alive.

expand to see more

SUSTAIN, v.t. To bear; to uphold; to support; as, a foundation sustains the superstructure.

2. To hold; to keep from falling; as, a rope sustains a weight.

3. To keep from sinking in despondence; to support.

4. To maintain; to keep alive; to support; to subsist; to nourish; as, provisions to sustain a family.

Key Scripture

Psa 55:22 — "Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved."

1Ki 17:9 — "Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee."

Neh 9:21 — "Yea, forty years didst thou sustain them in the wilderness, so that they lacked nothing; their clothes waxed not old, and their feet swelled not."

Pro 18:14 — "The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; but a wounded spirit who can bear?"

Psa 3:5 — "I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me."

Modern Corruption

Psalm 55:22 is read as a promise that the righteous will not be afflicted, and it promises they will not be moved.

expand to see more

David wrote Psalm 55 betrayed by his friend and fleeing his son, and the verse Peter quotes from it does not promise the removal of either. Cast thy burden upon the LORD — the burden is real and stays a burden — and He shall sustain thee: hold thee up under it. The second clause is the one that gets misquoted: He shall never suffer the righteous to be moved, which is a different thing from never suffering them to be afflicted. The sustained man is still carrying; he is not falling. First Kings 17:9 shows the means God is willing to use: a Gentile widow with a handful of meal, commanded to sustain a prophet, and the prophet sustained by a barrel that did not waste. Providence sustains through instruments that could not sustain themselves, and Nehemiah 9:21 records forty years of it — they lacked nothing — in a place where there was nothing.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew kul, pilpel (H3557), to contain, sustain, provide for; samak (H5564), to uphold, lean upon.

expand to see more

Hebrew kul, pilpel (H3557) — to sustain, nourish; Psalm 55:22, 1 Kings 17:9, Nehemiah 9:21, Genesis 27:37, Proverbs 18:14.

Hebrew samak (H5564) — to uphold, sustain; Psalm 3:5, Isaiah 59:16, Psalm 37:17.

Usage

"“Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee” — held up under it, not relieved of it."

"“I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee” — providence through a barrel."

"“A wounded spirit who can bear?” — the limit of a man's own sustaining."
